subject: Priv deployment: license boundary + fallback/playbook clarification

Subject: Priv deployment: license boundary + fallback/playbook clarification

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. As we start the procurement/legal loop I wanted to surface two items our InfoSec and procurement teams flagged so we can make sure the MSA + Order Form and the Private Deployment appendix line up:

1) License and usage boundary: we need the MSA to explicitly state whether the customer license for the private deployment is limited to "production workload only" (no dev/test) and whether any incidental replication (disaster recovery snapshots) is covered or treated as a separate licensed instance.

2) Fallback / controlled handover: our procurement team wants a short, audited rollback and operator-handover playbook in case of contract termination or a failover scenario. We're not asking for source code escrow, but we do need a defensible, auditable process for snapshot transfer + verification and operator credentials handoff for a staged transfer.

Can you connect me to the right legal lead at Redwood to discuss redlines? If you have a draft of the Private Deployment appendix or a proposed runbook we can share with our compliance team, that would speed things up.

Attachments: MSA_v2_Medsys_Redlines.pdf (pdf)

Thanks —
Emma

Emma — thanks for laying this out clearly. Tagging Laura (legal) and Rishi (lead on the commercials) so we can get you a consolidated response and a clean draft you can circulate internally.

Short answer up front: we can scope the customer license to production-only for the private deployment (Order Form exhibit) and provide a documented snapshot/handback workflow that does not involve source escrow. That said, the legal language and the operational checklist will require a couple of clarifying points from Medsys so our engineering/ops runbook maps to your audit expectations.

Laura — items to weigh in on: 1) whether the snapshot handover should require attestation (signed receipt) + optional remote validation window, 2) limits on our operator access during the transfer period, 3) any retention or forensic snapshot obligations Medsys needs to impose in the MSA. I've attached the internal draft appendix (PrivDeploy_ControlAppendix_draft.docx) — it's a working draft.

Emma — we aim to get an initial legal/ops response by EOD tomorrow. Can you confirm if Medsys requires encrypted transfer to a specific KMS or if a staged SFTP transfer is acceptable? Also, are there SLA carveouts you need for the transfer window?

—Marissa

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Priv deployment: license boundary + fallback/playbook clarification

Hi Emma / Marissa / Rishi —

Thanks for the context. I reviewed the draft appendix and the redlines Emma shared. High level thoughts and proposed edits below — I'm including suggested language snippets in-line so your counsel can take them directly into the MSA/Exhibit: 

A) License scope (Order Form / Exhibit A):
- Recommend explicit production-only clause: "Customer's license to deploy the Redwood runtime in Customer-managed infrastructure under this Order Form is limited to production workloads; separate development, test, staging, or DR environments require additional licensing unless expressly covered in the Order Form."
- Clarify replication/snapshots: treat DR replicas as governed by the same license only if they sit behind the same single-tenant VPC and are not used for parallel production workloads. Otherwise they should be listed as additional instances.

B) Snapshot & handover (escrow-like, but not source code):
- We can offer a documented, auditable snapshot transfer process: vendor generates an encrypted VM/snapshot, provides hash + manifest, performs a joint checksum validation during a scheduled handover window, and transfers via customer-provided KMS or an SFTP endpoint.
- Proposed clause: "Upon contract termination or upon Customer's written request for handover, Redwood will prepare operational snapshots and metadata and transfer them to Customer in encrypted form within 30 days, subject to any outstanding invoices. Redwood will provide verification artifacts (hash manifests) and a one-time remote validation window (3 business days) to confirm integrity."
- Limit operator access: during any transfer window Redwood shall only perform operations required to create the snapshot; no remote admin shell access shall be provided without a separate, time-bound escalation and audit trail.

C) Audit / verification and evidence:
- Add a short audit window: "Customer may request a single audit event to validate snapshot integrity and operational controls; all audit scope must be mutually agreed and scheduled with 15 business days' notice."
- For high-sensitivity customers, we can add a runbook exhibit describing steps, logs to capture, and acceptance criteria.

D) Commercial/compliance redlines to note:
- We will not accept language that requires transfer of source code or internal build artifacts.
- We prefer 'operator-assisted snapshot' wording over 'vendor access to customer systems' to reduce ongoing access obligations.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa, share the PrivDeploy appendix draft with Emma (I commented inline).
2) Emma — confirm whether Medsys needs transfer encrypted to their KMS ARN (preferred) or if SFTP to a hardened endpoint is acceptable; also confirm whether DR replicas are considered active production for Medsys' use case.
3) If Medsys wants an expanded audit, please provide a short bullet list of what success looks like for the transfer (e.g., hash validation, log delivery, runbook sign-off).

I can turn these bullets into tracked redlines for the MSA/Exhibit this week and hand the redlined doc to your counsel.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
